nodes.lazaret.options.[r_swoi].text.t: Are the Imperials from the field with you?

nodes.lazaret.options.[r_wszyscy].text.t: Have the wagons from the field come in yet?

nodes.lazaret.text.t: The healer wipes her hands on an apron that stopped being white long ago. "Sit wherever there's room, because there won't be for long. Dressing, drops, stitching: all at a price. Free, you can only die."

nodes.leczenie.text.t: The healer works fast and without questions. She pinches, stitches, wraps, says "don't move" three times and "good lad" once. Three-quarters of an hour later you walk out patched like a banner, but in one piece.

nodes.ranni.text.t: "More than beds, fewer than needed. Imperials, Jarnowians, locals, they all bleed the same and curse the same." She shrugs. "If one of your jobs takes you to the field, bring them to me before the crows finish counting."

nodes.ranni_lupy.text.t: The healer looks at your hands, then at your pouch. "You came back from the field lighter by a conscience and heavier by other people's things." She turns to the wounded man. "Dressings cost. You get no discount from me."

nodes.ranni_swoi.text.t: "Only the ones in red. You took them, you laid them down, obediently." The healer doesn't look up from the bandage. "The rest were left to the crows. I'm not saying it was wrong. I'm saying I count."

nodes.ranni_wszyscy.text.t: "All of them, no questions about uniforms. Half a day, three wagons and my captain looking at me as if I'd lost my mind. I haven't. Thank you." She wipes her hands on her apron. "If you see the field again, you know where to find me."
